## Purpose and scope

This protocol prepares Illumina amplicon libraries from bulk soil fauna DNA extracts for DNA metabarcoding: a fragment of the mitochondrial COI gene for microarthropods, and a fragment of the 18S rRNA gene for nematodes. It starts from DNA extracts (EnGeL-MOLB-DNA-MAG or -DNA-COL) and ends with a pooled, quantified library diluted to 4 nM for short-read sequencing. Bioinformatic processing is described in EnGeL-BIOINF-OBITOOLS4. Other markers can be added to the Primer table once validated.

## Principle

A first PCR amplifies the target region with fusion primers that carry a TruSeq-type (iTru) Illumina adapter overhang and 0–3 extra bases (“phased” primers) to increase sequence diversity at the start of the reads. A second, short PCR adds unique dual indexes and the P5/P7 adapters, so every sample can be identified after sequencing. Each indexed PCR product is cleaned with magnetic beads, quantified and normalised; the products are pooled, the pool is cleaned again and checked on the TapeStation, and its molar concentration is measured by qPCR before dilution for sequencing (Elbrecht et al., 2019; Glenn et al., 2019a, b; Porazinska et al., 2009).


![Two-step PCR and final library structure (iTru system). PCR1 adds the iTru overhang and 0–3 phasing bases to the template-specific primers; PCR2 adds the i5/i7 indexes and the P5/P7 adapters. Not to scale; sizes from the Primer table. Figure: EnGeL-UC, CC BY 4.0.](../../assets/figures/MB_library_structure.svg){#fig-mb-library fig-alt="Diagram of three DNA molecules: the template with forward and reverse primer sites; the PCR1 product with overhang, phasing bases, primer, target, primer, phasing bases, overhang; the final library with P5, i5 index, overhang, primer, target, primer, overhang, i7 index and P7." width="100%"}

### Primer table

<!-- bench -->
**Markers and PCR settings.**

| | COI (microarthropods) | 18S rRNA (nematodes) |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Primers (target-specific, 5′–3′) | BF3 `CCHGAYATRGCHTTYCCHCG` (Elbrecht et al., 2019); BR2 `TCDGGRTGNCCRAARAAYCA` (Elbrecht & Leese, 2017) | NF1 `GGTGGTGCATGGCCGTTCTTAGTT`; 18Sr2b `TACAAAGGGCAGGGACGTAAT` (Porazinska et al., 2009) |
| Target length (excluding primers) | c. 418 bp | 237–471 bp, mean c. 320 bp (Ficetola et al., 2024) |
| DNA input for PCR1 | Undiluted; dilute with nuclease-free water only if PCR inhibition is suspected | Diluted to 25–35 ng/µL (suggested 35 ng/µL) |
| PCR1 annealing | 50 °C, 90 s | 60 °C, 90 s |
| Expected size after PCR1 / PCR2 | c. 525 bp / c. 595 bp | c. 350–585 bp / c. 420–650 bp |
| Pool clean-up bead ratio (pool : beads) | 1:0.65 | 1:0.75 (0.65× may remove short amplicons and bias the community) |
| Read overlap with 2 × 250 bp | c. 40 bp, enough to merge | Most amplicons merge; the longest (up to 471 bp + c. 45 bp primers) do not; 2 × 300 bp would cover the full range |

### First-PCR primers with overhang (5′–3′)

Overhang (P5 side): `ACACTCTTTCCCTACACGACGCTCTTCCGATCT`; overhang (P7 side): `GTGACTGGAGTTCAGACGTGTGCTCTTCCGATCT`. Phased versions add 0–3 bases between overhang and primer (ins0–ins3) to increase sequence diversity at the start of the reads. These TruSeq-type (iTru) overhangs are the binding sites of the iTru index primers used in the second PCR.

| Name | Sequence |
|:--|:--|
| iTru_COI_BF3_P5_ins0 | `ACACTCTTTCCCTACACGACGCTCTTCCGATCTCCHGAYATRGCHTTYCCHCG` |
| iTru_COI_BF3_P5_ins1 | `ACACTCTTTCCCTACACGACGCTCTTCCGATCTACCHGAYATRGCHTTYCCHCG` |
| iTru_COI_BF3_P5_ins2 | `ACACTCTTTCCCTACACGACGCTCTTCCGATCTGACCHGAYATRGCHTTYCCHCG` |
| iTru_COI_BF3_P5_ins3 | `ACACTCTTTCCCTACACGACGCTCTTCCGATCTTGACCHGAYATRGCHTTYCCHCG` |
| iTru_COI_BR2_P7_ins0 | `GTGACTGGAGTTCAGACGTGTGCTCTTCCGATCTCDGGRTGNCCRAARAAYCA` |
| iTru_COI_BR2_P7_ins1 | `GTGACTGGAGTTCAGACGTGTGCTCTTCCGATCTTCDGGRTGNCCRAARAAYCA` |
| iTru_COI_BR2_P7_ins2 | `GTGACTGGAGTTCAGACGTGTGCTCTTCCGATCTATCDGGRTGNCCRAARAAYCA` |
| iTru_COI_BR2_P7_ins3 | `GTGACTGGAGTTCAGACGTGTGCTCTTCCGATCTGATCDGGRTGNCCRAARAAYCA` |
| iTru_NF1_P5_ins0 | `ACACTCTTTCCCTACACGACGCTCTTCCGATCTGGTGGTGCATGGCCGTTCTTAGTT` |
| iTru_NF1_P5_ins1 | `ACACTCTTTCCCTACACGACGCTCTTCCGATCTAGGTGGTGCATGGCCGTTCTTAGTT` |
| iTru_NF1_P5_ins2 | `ACACTCTTTCCCTACACGACGCTCTTCCGATCTGAGGTGGTGCATGGCCGTTCTTAGTT` |
| iTru_NF1_P5_ins3 | `ACACTCTTTCCCTACACGACGCTCTTCCGATCTTGAGGTGGTGCATGGCCGTTCTTAGTT` |
| iTru_18Sr2b_P7_ins0 | `GTGACTGGAGTTCAGACGTGTGCTCTTCCGATCTTACAAAGGGCAGGGACGTAAT` |
| iTru_18Sr2b_P7_ins1 | `GTGACTGGAGTTCAGACGTGTGCTCTTCCGATCTTTACAAAGGGCAGGGACGTAAT` |
| iTru_18Sr2b_P7_ins2 | `GTGACTGGAGTTCAGACGTGTGCTCTTCCGATCTATTACAAAGGGCAGGGACGTAAT` |
| iTru_18Sr2b_P7_ins3 | `GTGACTGGAGTTCAGACGTGTGCTCTTCCGATCTGATTACAAAGGGCAGGGACGTAAT` |

**Second-PCR index primers:** iTru_i5_P5 `AATGATACGGCGACCACCGAGATCTACAC[i5 index]ACACTCTTTCCCTAC`; iTru_i7_P7 `CAAGCAGAAGACGGCATACGAGAT[i7 index]GTGACTGGAGTTCAG`. Adapterama iTru5/iTru7 primers (Glenn et al., 2019a): 384 unique dual-index pairs on four 96-well plates (1–384); index names and sequences are in the primer workbooks and the index sheets of the Lab Pipeline workbook.

## Reagent preparation

- **First-PCR primers (with overhang):** 10 µM working solutions [TO CONFIRM: how the phased versions ins0–ins3 are combined, e.g. equimolar mix per direction; storage].
- **iTru index primers:** synthesised at 25 nmol scale, standard desalting, with one phosphorothioate bond; diluted to 5 µM and aliquoted in strip tubes (primer workbook) [TO CONFIRM: storage].
- **Ethanol 80%:** prepare fresh on the day.
- **KAPA Pure Beads:** equilibrate to room temperature and vortex c. 30 s before use.

## Procedure

### Before starting

{{< include ../../includes/_contamination-control.qmd >}}
- Prepare or update the plate map and index assignment (Annex 1) and the project's Lab Pipeline workbook.
- Include a PCR negative control (water) on each plate and, whenever possible, a positive control per run (a mock community of known composition). Extraction blanks from the DNA extraction are carried through. Every control gets its own index combination and is sequenced.

### First PCR (amplicon PCR)

(@) Prepare the DNA input for the marker (Primer table): COI — undiluted; 18S — diluted to 25–35 ng/µL with nuclease-free water.
(@) Set up one 10 µL reaction per sample: 5 µL Qiagen Multiplex PCR Master Mix, 1 µL of each primer with overhang (10 µM), 2 µL nuclease-free water and 1 µL of DNA. Up to 3 µL of DNA may be used for low-concentration extracts, reducing the water so that the volume stays at 10 µL.
(@) Cycling: 95 °C for 15 min; 25 cycles of 94 °C for 30 s, annealing for 90 s (COI 50 °C; 18S 60 °C), 72 °C for 90 s; final extension 72 °C for 10 min.
(@) Check amplification on a 2% agarose gel. All field samples should show bands of the expected size; extraction and PCR negative controls should show no amplification. Record the outcome per well (Gel_Success, Faint, Failure, Lost, Pending) in the Lab Pipeline workbook.

### Second PCR (indexing PCR)

(@) Set up one 14 µL reaction per sample: 7 µL KAPA HiFi HotStart ReadyMix, 0.7 µL iTru5 index primer (5 µM), 0.7 µL iTru7 index primer (5 µM), 2.8 µL nuclease-free water and 2.8 µL of first-PCR product. Record the index plate and well of every sample in the plate map.

::: {.callout-important title="CRITICAL"}
Each sample in a pool must carry a unique iTru5/iTru7 index combination. Combinations must never be repeated within the same pool: duplicated combinations cannot be demultiplexed. Check the plate map against the indexes actually used.
:::

(@) Cycling: 95 °C for 3 min; 8 cycles of 95 °C for 30 s, 55 °C for 30 s, 72 °C for 30 s; final elongation 72 °C for 5 min.

### Clean-up of individual PCR products (KAPA Pure Beads, 0.7×)

(@) Transfer 10 µL of each indexing PCR product to a new U-bottom 96-well plate.
(@) Vortex the KAPA Pure Beads (room temperature) for c. 30 s. Add 7 µL of beads per well (1:0.7, product : beads), pipetting into the bottom of the well. For a full plate, dispense from a PCR strip (e.g. 91 µL per strip tube for a row of 12 wells plus excess) and re-vortex the beads every 3 columns. Use 20 µL filter tips.
(@) Mix by pipetting up and down 10–12 times without bubbles; incubate for 5 min at room temperature.
(@) Meanwhile, prepare three U-bottom plates: two wash plates with 150 µL of freshly prepared 80% ethanol per well, and one elution plate with 30 µL of elution buffer per well.
(@) Place the magnetic extractor on the bead plate, let the beads collect (c. 2–3 min), then lift the beads.
(@) Wash: place the extractor in the first wash plate for 30 s, then in the second for 30 s.
(@) Air-dry the beads on the extractor for 30–60 s (no longer than 2–3 min). Do not over-dry: this makes elution harder.
(@) Elute: place the extractor in the elution plate, release the beads and leave them to resuspend for 5 min (optional: 5 min at 55 °C to improve recovery). Re-attach the magnet to remove the beads; the cleaned products stay in the elution plate.
(@) Optional (recommended): check c. 1 µL on an agarose gel or the TapeStation for a single band of the expected size (Primer table) and no primer dimers (< 150 bp).

::: {.callout-note title="NOTE"}
At the end of a bead tube, spin it down and transfer the remainder to a new tube rather than using it directly, as it may no longer be homogeneous; vortex the new tube well.
:::

### Quantification, normalisation and pooling

(@) Measure the concentration of each cleaned product by fluorometry (Qubit dsDNA HS or PicoGreen; EnGeL-MOLB-NAQC) and record the values in the plate map.
(@) Normalise each product to 20 nM with nuclease-free water or 10 mM Tris-HCl, using the measured concentration and the expected fragment size (Calculations; *PCR2_Plate* sheet of the Lab Pipeline workbook). Mix gently.
(@) Combine the normalised products into one tube to make the pooled library (*Pooling* sheet). Check the plate map before pooling and label and document the samples and indexes in each pool.

### Clean-up of the pooled library

(@) Add KAPA Pure Beads to the pool at the ratio for the marker (Primer table: COI 1:0.65; 18S 1:0.75).
(@) Mix by vortexing and incubate for 10 min at room temperature.
(@) Place the tube on a magnetic stand for 5 min; remove and discard the supernatant without disturbing the beads.
(@) Wash the beads twice with 200 µL of freshly prepared 80% ethanol for 60 s. Remove the ethanol completely and air-dry for 3–5 min (do not over-dry).
(@) Remove the tube from the magnet and resuspend the beads in 200 µL of elution buffer (10 mM Tris-HCl, pH 8.0–8.5, or low-TE). Incubate for 5–10 min at room temperature. The elution volume sets the final concentration: use less to concentrate low-yield pools, more to dilute, keeping enough for TapeStation, qPCR and sequencing.
(@) Place the tube on the magnetic stand for 5 min and transfer the eluate (cleaned pool) to a clean tube.

### Pooled library check on the TapeStation (D1000)

(@) Take the D1000 ScreenTape and reagents from 4 °C and equilibrate to room temperature for 30 min; keep the ScreenTape in its pouch, protected from light.
(@) Ladder: mix 3 µL D1000 Sample Buffer + 1 µL D1000 Ladder in the first tube or well. Samples: mix 3 µL D1000 Sample Buffer + 1 µL library.
(@) Seal with caps or foil, vortex and centrifuge briefly.
(@) Insert the ScreenTape and the tubes into the TapeStation; remove caps or foil and check that the tip box is full. Run.
(@) Confirm a single peak at the expected size and no primer/adapter dimers. If dimers persist, repeat the pool clean-up. Record the average fragment size.

### Library quantification by qPCR (KAPA)

Quantify the cleaned pool with the KAPA Library Quantification Kit, as in EnGeL-MOLB-KAPA:

{{< include ../../includes/_kapa-qpcr.qmd >}}

### Dilution to 4 nM and submission

(@) Calculate the library concentration (Calculations) and dilute the library to 4 nM with an appropriate buffer [TO CONFIRM: buffer]. Mix gently.
(@) Prepare the sequencing submission from the *Novogene_Submission* sheet of the Lab Pipeline workbook (sequencer choice sets the i5 orientation) and the provider's sample information form [TO CONFIRM: provider and form for each project].

::: {.callout-tip title="PAUSE POINT"}
Cleaned PCR products and the pooled library can be stored at [TO CONFIRM: −20 °C?] between steps.
:::

### After finishing

## Calculations

**Normalisation to 20 nM** (as in the Lab Pipeline workbook):

$$c_\mathrm{nM} = \frac{c_\mathrm{ng}}{0.00066 \times L}$$

$$V_\mathrm{water} = V_\mathrm{p} \times \left(\frac{c_\mathrm{nM}}{20} - 1\right)$$

- $c_\mathrm{nM}$: molar concentration of the PCR product (nM)
- $c_\mathrm{ng}$: mass concentration measured by fluorometry (ng/µL)
- $L$: fragment size (bp); 0.00066: mass of 1 nmol of 1 bp of dsDNA (µg), as used in the workbook
- $V_\mathrm{p}$: volume of PCR product (µL); $V_\mathrm{water}$: volume of water or 10 mM Tris-HCl to add (µL)

**Worked example** (illustrative values): 15 ng/µL, 620 bp → 15 / (0.00066 × 620) = 36.7 nM; for 10 µL of product add 10 × (36.7 / 20 − 1) = 8.3 µL to reach 20 nM.

**Library concentration by qPCR**

{{< include ../../includes/_kapa-calculation.qmd >}}

**Dilution of the pool for loading:** dilution factor = pool concentration (nM) / target concentration (nM); volume of pool = required volume / dilution factor; buffer = required volume − volume of pool (*Pooling* sheet).

## Quality control

| Control | Where | Purpose | Acceptance criterion |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Extraction blanks | Carried from the DNA extraction | Contamination during extraction | No band on the PCR1 gel; contaminant reads removed in bioinformatics |
| PCR negative (water) | Each PCR plate | Contamination during PCR | No band on the PCR1 gel |
| Positive control / mock community | Each run, whenever possible | PCR and sequencing performance | [TO CONFIRM] |
| PCR1 gel | Every sample | Amplification | Band of the expected size (Primer table) |
| Cleaned product check (optional) | Subset or all | Size and dimers | Single band of the expected size; no dimers < 150 bp |
| Pooled library (TapeStation) | Each pool | Size and dimers | Single peak at the expected size; no primer/adapter dimers |
| qPCR run | Each quantification | Reliable concentration | See table below |

**qPCR run acceptance**

{{< include ../../includes/_kapa-run-qc.qmd >}}

## Data and metadata

- **Outputs:** gel images; concentrations; pooled library with TapeStation trace and qPCR concentration; after sequencing, paired fastq files (R1, R2) per sample.
- **Sequencing:** Illumina NovaSeq, 2 × 250 bp paired-end, at least 30 000 reads per sample.
- **Where:** the project's Metabarcoding Lab Pipeline workbook (*Sample_Tracking*, *PCR1_Plate*, *PCR2_Plate*, *Pooling*, *Library_QC*, *Novogene_Submission*), the plate map and the lab book. Sequence data are deposited in [TO CONFIRM: public archive, e.g. ENA].

::: {.callout-note title="Minimum to record"}
- EnGeL label of each DNA extract; plate ID and well; sample type (sample, extraction blank, PCR negative, mock)
- Marker and primer pair; PCR1 and PCR2 plate IDs, dates, operators and thermocycler; PCR outcomes (Gel_Success, Estimated_Success, Faint, Failure, Lost, Pending)
- Index plate and well, iTru5 and iTru7 index names and sequences; pool ID
- Lot numbers: Qiagen Multiplex PCR Master Mix, KAPA HiFi HotStart ReadyMix, KAPA Pure Beads, KAPA Library Quantification Kit; primer and index plate IDs
- Concentrations after clean-up; normalisation volumes; TapeStation size; qPCR concentration; final dilution
- MIxS fields for the sequence submission [TO CONFIRM: checklist and package, e.g. MIMARKS-survey]
:::

## Safety and waste

{{< include ../../includes/_safety-general.qmd >}}

- DNA intercalating dyes: handle with gloves [TO CONFIRM against the SDS].
- Gel imaging: protect eyes and skin from UV light.
{{< include ../../includes/_safety-ethanol.qmd >}}

**Waste**

{{< include ../../includes/_waste-streams.qmd >}}

For this protocol: gels and gel-contaminated material [TO CONFIRM: route]; PCR plates, bead plates, tips and tubes to biological solid waste (black bin); bead supernatants and ethanol washes [TO CONFIRM: route].

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | Likely cause | Solution |
|:--|:--|:--|
| No band after PCR1 (COI) | PCR inhibition | Dilute the DNA extract with nuclease-free water and repeat. |
| Band in a negative control | Contamination | [TO CONFIRM: repeat the plate? sequence and filter?] |
| Primer/adapter dimers in the pool | Incomplete clean-up | Repeat the pool clean-up. |
| Low recovery after bead clean-up | Beads over-dried, or not homogeneous | Dry for no longer than 2–3 min; vortex beads; transfer the end of a bead tube to a new tube. |
| Tips clog when dispensing beads | 10 µL tips | Use 20 µL filter tips. |
| Samples cannot be demultiplexed | Index combination repeated in the pool | Check the plate map before pooling; each combination once per pool. |

## Remarks

The Metabarcoding Lab Pipeline workbook is the working record for this protocol: one copy per project. Its built-in PCR calculator (25 µL, 2× master mix) is for standard PCRs, not for these metabarcoding reactions. The adapter and index system is the one used in the lab (FAVIS primer workbooks; BENCHMARKS mesofauna 2024 runs): TruSeq-type (iTru) phased primers and Adapterama iTru5/iTru7 indexes. The BENCHMARKS handbook (D4.3) describes Nextera-type overhangs with iNext indexes instead; the two systems are not interchangeable (iTru indexes need the iTru overhang, iNext indexes the Nextera-type overhang).

4. Storage of PCR products and pools between steps; buffer for the 4 nM dilution.
5. Sequencing provider and form per project; public archive for the data; MIxS checklist.
6. Waste routes for gels, bead supernatants and ethanol washes; intercalating dye hazards.
7. Hands-on and total time.
8. DOI.

## Annex 1 – Plate map guidance {.unnumbered}

{{< include ../../includes/_plate-map.qmd >}}

**Index assignment**

- Each well must have a unique iTru5/iTru7 combination within a pool. A simple scheme is one iTru5 index per row and one iTru7 index per column, giving 96 unique combinations per plate.
- When several plates are pooled together, each plate must use a different index set, so that no combination is repeated within the pool.
- Check the plate map against the indexes actually used before pooling.
